UEFA has launched a probe into violent clashes that marred Europa League fixtures involving Marseille and Besiktas, European football’s governing body announced on Friday. Several hundred Marseille fans confronted visiting Levski Sofia supporters on Thursday, while a diplomatic incident was sparked by the Georgian police’s response to Besiktas supporters unfurling a pro-Palestinian banner during their match with Israeli side Hapoel Beer-Sheva. “The events witnessed at the above-mentioned matches run counter… to UEFA’s objective, enshrined in its Statutes, of ensuring that football matches are played in a spirit of peace, mutual respect and sporting fairness,” said UEFA. “UEFA has appointed Ethics and Disciplinary Inspectors to conduct disciplinary investigations into the incidents.” Magistrates in Marseille are conducting their own probe into “intentional violence” from a section of the southern club’s home support, which ended in five Levski Sofia fans being hospitalised. That match had been moved to Georgia after Turkish authorities informed UEFA that, “for safety and security reasons”, the match could not be hosted in Istanbul.
